page_title: balenaEtcher - Flash OS images to SD cards & USB drives

sources.entry: Etcher - Flash OS images to SD cards & USB drives, safely and easily. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/balena-io/etcher) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: balenaEtcher
summary.one_liner: A free, open source, cross-platform app that flashes OS images (such as ISOs and SD card images) onto SD cards and USB drives.
use_cases: Flashing a Raspberry Pi or other board OS image to an SD card
Creating bootable USB installation media from an ISO
Installing an OS image onto a USB flash drive
Letting end users flash your OS from your website with a button
Verifying a flashed card boots and is not corrupted
summary.what_it_does: Etcher writes OS image files to SD cards and USB drives through a three-step graphical process with no command line needed. It warns users and hides system drives by default to reduce the risk of wiping the wrong disk. After writing, it confirms the flash completed. It can flash images from a URL or a local file. The page also describes a 'Flash with Etcher' button that sites can add to let their users flash an OS directly. Packages are offered for Windows, Linux (including .deb and .rpm) and macOS.
notable: Hides system drives by default and warns before erasing to prevent wiping the wrong drive
Verifies that the flash completed successfully
Offers a 'Flash with Etcher' button for embedding on websites
Built with JS, HTML, Node.js and Electron; open source on GitHub
caveats: Windows images are not bootable with Etcher without extra steps; it is not designed for that
Windows 7, 8 or 32-bit systems are limited to Etcher v7.9.0
Etcher erases the entire target drive when flashing
